name: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe
description: Yirgacheffe is a well-known coffee-growing region in southern Ethiopia. Coffees from this area are valued for their light, aromatic profile and bright acidity. They work especially well with filter brewing, which brings out delicate flavor notes.

name: Colombia Huila
description: Colombia is one of the best-known producers of Arabica, and Huila is one of the country’s leading coffee-growing regions. The beans have a balanced, sweet profile that works well both as filter coffee and in milk-based drinks.

name: Brazil Santos
description: Brazil is the world’s largest coffee producer. Brazilian beans often have a soft nutty and chocolatey profile with moderate acidity. They are commonly used for espresso and milk-based drinks.

name: Kenya AA
description: AA is a size grade in the Kenyan coffee classification, referring to large beans. Kenyan coffees are often described as juicy, with bright acidity and berry notes.

name: Vietnam Robusta
description: Vietnam is one of the world’s largest robusta producers. Robusta is usually stronger and more bitter than Arabica and contains more caffeine. It is often added to espresso blends.

name: Espresso blend
origin: Blend of beans from several regions
description: A blend is a mix of coffee beans from different regions or varieties. The beans are selected to create a balanced flavor and consistent results when brewing espresso.

name: Guatemala Antigua
description: Antigua is a well-known coffee-growing region in Guatemala, located in a valley surrounded by volcanoes. Coffees from this area are often described as balanced, with chocolate and spicy notes.

name: Costa Rica Tarrazú
description: Tarrazú is one of Costa Rica’s best-known coffee-growing regions, where coffee is grown at high elevations. Coffees from this area usually have a clean flavor and lively acidity.

name: Indonesia Sumatra Mandheling
description: Coffee from Sumatra often has a full body, earthy notes and low acidity. These beans are known for a distinctive processing method called wet-hulling.

name: India Monsooned Malabar
description: Monsooned Malabar is an Indian coffee whose beans are exposed to humid monsoon winds. This process changes the flavor profile: acidity decreases and the coffee develops a heavier body.

name: Philippines Liberica (Barako)
description: Liberica is a less common coffee species than Arabica and Robusta. In the Philippines, a well-known local type of Liberica is called Barako; it is usually described as strong and aromatic.
